answer: A deposit-backed identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable stake to register one identity, and the stake is slashed if that identity is caught duplicating work or voting twice. A meadow of cheap fake accounts cannot bloom when every identity costs real collateral, just as a marble floor stays level only when each tile is laid once and checked. Verified behavior earns the stake back over time, like velvet that only softens with honest use, while abusers lose their deposit and their seat.
